description: U.S. residents aged 0–7 (age-distribution category 0–14), including infants and very young children whose needs and activities are caregiver-shaped; no independent leisure interests, reading, cooking, work, or public-opinion profile is imposed.
U.S. residents aged 8–14 (age-distribution category 0–14); this child/caregiver band leaves independent interests, reading, cooking, work, and public-opinion profiles open.
U.S. residents aged 15–17 (age-distribution category 15–24); retains the younger part of this age group without assigning adult education, marital, labor-force, or public-opinion profiles.
U.S. residents aged 18–24 (age-distribution category 15–24); adult opinions and habits remain open to the supplied alternatives, with weighted demographic choices retained.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), with little or interrupted formal schooling and compatible lower educational attainment; all other supplied demographic choices remain available.

selected.education_attainment: Has not completed high school, representing approximately 10% of the supplied population figures; may include people with limited formal schooling, interrupted schooling, or literacy support needs.
selected.education_and_learning_profile: Has had little or interrupted access to formal schooling and may have very limited literacy or numeracy, while retaining practical knowledge and skills learned through daily life.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), with advanced educational attainment and the supplied highly accomplished researcher or specialist learning profile; demographic options otherwise remain open.

selected.education_attainment: Has a bachelor's degree or a higher qualification, including people with professional, master's, doctoral, or other advanced education; approximately 35% under the supplied totals.
selected.education_and_learning_profile: Is a highly accomplished researcher, physician, engineer, scholar, or other specialist who contributes advanced expertise and may teach or mentor others.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a warm, cooperative, considerate personality profile; other personality dimensions and weighted demographics are not restricted.

selected.personality_traits: Is warm, cooperative, and considerate, readily offering practical help while still being capable of setting boundaries when needed.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated the unusually cynical or antagonistic personality extreme; weighted demographics and political views remain unrestricted.

selected.personality_traits: Is unusually cynical or antagonistic, expecting bad faith from others and sometimes behaving unkindly or manipulatively; this describes a rare extreme rather than a typical trait.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a strongly progressive political-belief profile; party affiliation and other demographic choices retain their supplied alternatives.

selected.political_beliefs: Strongly progressive, prioritizing reductions in inequality, broad access to healthcare and education, civil rights protections, and robust public action on climate and social needs.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a strongly conservative political-belief profile; party affiliation and other demographic choices retain their supplied alternatives.

selected.political_beliefs: Strongly conservative, placing high importance on tradition, religious or cultural continuity, gun rights, national sovereignty, and substantially limited government.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a strongly optimistic and encouraging general-attitude profile; no political, personality, or demographic category is inferred from it.

selected.general_attitude: Approaches daily life with strong optimism, expects setbacks to be manageable, and actively encourages other people through generous and hopeful conversation.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a persistently pessimistic general-attitude profile.

selected.general_attitude: Is persistently pessimistic, focuses on likely failure and disappointment, and may discount positive developments as temporary or undeserved.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated an open-minded and curious general-attitude profile.

selected.general_attitude: Is open-minded and curious, listens to unfamiliar viewpoints, and can revise an opinion when new evidence or personal experience gives a persuasive reason.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated the unusually hostile and closed-minded general-attitude extreme.

selected.general_attitude: Is unusually hostile and closed-minded, reacts to disagreement with contempt or aggression, and may deliberately undermine or mistreat others; this is an extreme fringe profile.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this illustrative profile combines traditional home cooking, deliberate infrequent shopping, health-focused habits, openness to new products, local cultural influences, frequent travel, and an active lifestyle. Demographic choices remain weighted and unconstrained.

selected.culinary_tastes: Prefers familiar, traditional home cooking, such as regional family recipes, straightforward sides, and meals tied to personal or community traditions.
selected.shopping_habits: Shops infrequently and deliberately, replacing items only when necessary and comparing prices carefully before committing to a purchase.
selected.health_consciousness: Is highly health-focused, schedules preventive care, exercises consistently, reads nutrition information, and makes daily choices with long-term wellbeing in mind.
selected.attitude_toward_new_products: Eagerly tests new products early, enjoys emerging technology and novel services, and tolerates occasional defects or inconvenience for the experience.
selected.cultural_influences: Is strongly shaped by local community traditions, neighborhood relationships, regional foodways, and customs passed among nearby generations.
selected.travel_habits: Travels frequently for work or leisure, is comfortable with airports and changing schedules, and often plans trips across the country or internationally.
selected.lifestyle: Maintains a highly active lifestyle with frequent walking, sports, outdoor recreation, and social commitments, adapting activity to health and access.
selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Follows a consistent health routine involving preventive appointments, sleep practices, exercise, and food choices that support personal wellbeing.
selected.technology_use: Uses smartphones, computers, online services, and social media frequently for work, communication, news, entertainment, and everyday tasks.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this contrasting profile includes adventurous food tastes, frequent shopping, an indulgent and sedentary routine, resistance to product changes, global influences, and preference for home-based recreation.

selected.culinary_tastes: Is adventurous about food, regularly tries unfamiliar cuisines, ingredients, and cooking techniques, and enjoys discussing how dishes reflect their cultural origins.
selected.shopping_habits: Shops frequently for household necessities and groceries, often planning lists and routines to manage a busy household or caregiving responsibilities.
selected.health_consciousness: Enjoys indulgent foods and a sedentary leisure routine, rarely prioritizes exercise, and may find health recommendations inconvenient or difficult to sustain.
selected.attitude_toward_new_products: Is strongly resistant to changes in routines and products, viewing many new offerings as unnecessary, confusing, or designed to create avoidable costs.
selected.cultural_influences: Is heavily influenced by global media, international travel, online communities, and popular culture from multiple countries rather than by a single local tradition.
selected.travel_habits: Is a homebody who finds comfort and enjoyment in familiar surroundings and chooses local recreation over overnight or international trips.
selected.lifestyle: Lives a mostly sedentary routine because of desk work, limited energy, disability, transportation needs, or preference for screen-based leisure.
selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Has low physical-activity engagement, perhaps because of time, health, mobility, safety, cost, access, motivation, or work constraints.
selected.technology_use: Experiences excessive or compulsive screen use that interferes with sleep, work, relationships, safety, or other daily responsibilities.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile contrasts bold, spicy food with in-store shopping, organic food preferences, cautious product evaluation, traditional cultural influences, adventurous trips, and minimalist living.

selected.culinary_tastes: Enjoys bold heat and strongly seasoned food, seeking hot peppers, spice blends, and cuisines where intense flavor is central to the meal.
selected.shopping_habits: Usually shops in physical stores to inspect products, ask questions, handle items, and combine errands with other activities.
selected.health_consciousness: Seeks organic, minimally processed, or locally sourced foods when affordable and accessible, while recognizing that practical constraints sometimes determine purchases.
selected.attitude_toward_new_products: Is cautious about product claims, checks safety, privacy, durability, and return policies, and avoids purchasing based only on marketing or hype.
selected.cultural_influences: Keeps traditional practices central to family life and is cautious about rapid cultural change, while still navigating contemporary workplaces and institutions.
selected.travel_habits: Seeks adventurous travel, outdoor challenges, unfamiliar places, and flexible itineraries, while preparing carefully for safety and practical needs.
selected.lifestyle: Prefers minimalist living, owns relatively few possessions, and values simplicity, low maintenance, financial restraint, or environmental impact.
selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Maintains regular physical activity through walking, exercise, sports, or other movement and tries to fit it into an otherwise busy schedule.
selected.technology_use: Uses digital technology confidently but sets limits on notifications, screen time, online shopping, or social media to protect attention and privacy.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile allows mild, simple flavors, online shopping, conventional health preferences, high novelty seeking, cosmopolitan cultural influences, and predictable comfortable travel.

selected.culinary_tastes: Prefers mild, simple flavors and may avoid hot spices, strong aromas, unfamiliar textures, or complicated combinations because they feel unpleasant or overwhelming.
selected.shopping_habits: Prefers online shopping for convenience, broad selection, accessibility, or time savings, and commonly checks reviews and delivery costs before buying.
selected.health_consciousness: Prefers conventional food and mainstream health advice, relies on familiar products, and is cautious about unverified supplements or wellness trends.
selected.attitude_toward_new_products: Is an extreme novelty seeker who buys untested products impulsively and disregards reasonable warnings, costs, or safety information.
selected.cultural_influences: Prefers contemporary and cosmopolitan cultural expression, regularly engaging with new music, art, ideas, and communities from around the world.
selected.travel_habits: Prefers comfortable, predictable travel with reservations, familiar lodging, accessible transportation, and enough time to avoid rushed transitions.
selected.lifestyle: Favors an extravagant lifestyle, frequently spending on luxury goods, premium experiences, or expansive homes, sometimes with little concern for restraint.
selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Has inconsistent routines, alternating periods of healthy intentions with long stretches when fatigue, stress, or responsibilities take priority.
selected.technology_use: Uses smartphones, computers, online services, and social media frequently for work, communication, news, entertainment, and everyday tasks.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile includes vegetarian food, budget-conscious shopping, a rare harmful health extreme, familiar homogeneous cultural surroundings, and local outings.

selected.culinary_tastes: Follows a vegetarian diet for ethical, religious, environmental, health, or personal reasons and seeks satisfying meals centered on vegetables, grains, beans, or dairy.
selected.shopping_habits: Plans purchases around a strict household budget, uses coupons or discount stores, and prioritizes durable essentials over optional upgrades.
selected.health_consciousness: Engages in potentially harmful extremes, such as severely restricting food, overexercising, or ignoring urgent health needs; this represents a rare and concerning edge case.
selected.attitude_toward_new_products: Avoids digital products and services when possible because of privacy concerns, accessibility barriers, limited connectivity, or low confidence using technology.
selected.cultural_influences: Has a mostly homogeneous cultural environment and feels comfortable with familiar customs, language, food, and social expectations.
selected.travel_habits: Enjoys short regional trips and day outings, preferring nearby parks, family visits, beaches, or small towns to long-distance travel.
selected.lifestyle: Lives a family-centered or caregiving-focused routine, organizing much of the day around children, older relatives, household tasks, or supportive relationships.
selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Is intensely focused on health in a rigid or distressing way, or conversely disregards serious symptoms and care needs; these are uncommon extremes.
selected.technology_use: Has limited digital access or skills because of cost, disability, connectivity, age, language, or lack of training, and may depend on others for online tasks.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile includes fully plant-based food, extravagant shopping, chronic health needs, layered cultural influences, and travel avoidance.

selected.culinary_tastes: Follows a fully plant-based diet, checking ingredients carefully and choosing meals that avoid meat, fish, dairy, eggs, and other animal products.
selected.shopping_habits: Is highly extravagant, making frequent luxury or impulse purchases with limited attention to long-term affordability; this is an uncommon extreme profile.
selected.health_consciousness: Lives with chronic illness, disability, pain, or mental health challenges that require substantial daily management, accommodations, medication, or support.
selected.attitude_toward_new_products: Prefers established brands and familiar products because consistency and predictability matter more than novelty or small possible improvements.
selected.cultural_influences: Moves among several cultural communities and adapts language, food, music, and social behavior to different family, work, or neighborhood settings.
selected.travel_habits: Avoids travel because of anxiety, safety concerns, sensory overload, unfamiliar environments, or past negative experiences, even when opportunities are available.
selected.lifestyle: Has a highly irregular lifestyle shaped by shift work, unstable housing, illness, crisis, or unpredictable obligations, making routines and leisure difficult to maintain.
selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Lives with a condition or disability that makes standard health recommendations difficult to follow and may require adapted care and realistic goals.
selected.technology_use: Avoids social media or online services because of privacy concerns, misinformation, harassment, scams, or a preference for offline interaction.

description: U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile includes meat-centered meals, brand-conscious shopping, limited opportunity for exercise, a trusted-recommendation approach to new products, and travel mainly for obligations.

selected.culinary_tastes: Enjoys meat-centered meals, values familiar preparations such as grilling or roasting, and may see meat as an important source of flavor, tradition, or nourishment.
selected.shopping_habits: Is brand-conscious and willing to pay more for familiar quality, customer service, design, or status, while still comparing some alternatives.
selected.health_consciousness: Has limited opportunity for exercise or preventive care because of cost, disability, demanding work, caregiving, transportation, or limited access to services.
selected.attitude_toward_new_products: Tries unfamiliar products when recommended by a trusted friend, relative, professional, or community member who understands their needs.
selected.cultural_influences: Feels culturally isolated or alienated, has limited access to community traditions or shared identity, and may be uncertain where they belong.
selected.travel_habits: Travels mainly to visit family, attend important events, or meet obligations, and does not necessarily consider travel a recreational interest.
selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Has limited access to primary care, nutritious food, safe exercise spaces, or reliable health information because of financial or geographic barriers.
selected.technology_use: Is enthusiastic about gaming, streaming, smart devices, or emerging digital tools and enjoys learning new features.

description: U.S. residents aged 55–64 (age-distribution category 55–64); supplied weighted demographic alternatives are retained, with a varied health-and-wellness habit profile.

selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Snacks frequently and often reaches for convenient foods such as cookies, reflecting preference, habit, stress, convenience, or availability.

description: U.S. residents aged 55–64 (age-distribution category 55–64); supplied weighted demographic alternatives are retained, with varied stress-management and coping habits.

selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Uses exercise, meditation, prayer, hobbies, or social support to manage stress and preserve emotional wellbeing.

description: U.S. residents aged 65–110 (age-distribution category 65 and older); the full supplied age range is retained, with varied stress-coping habits and no advanced-education restriction.

selected.health_and_wellness_habits: Copes with stress through comfort eating, smoking, inactivity, or other habits that may offer short-term relief but create longer-term concerns.

description: U.S. residents aged 65–110 (age-distribution category 65 and older); the supplied weighted demographics and broad attainment range are retained, alongside inconsistent wellness routines.

health_and_wellness_habits: Snacks frequently and often reaches for convenient foods such as cookies, reflecting preference, habit, stress, convenience, or availability.
Has inconsistent routines, alternating periods of healthy intentions with long stretches when fatigue, stress, or responsibilities take priority.
Copes with stress through comfort eating, smoking, inactivity, or other habits that may offer short-term relief but create longer-term concerns.
